extraction.methodology_summary: The authors construct a time-varying directed network of cryptocurrencies based on return cross-predictability (using adaptive Lasso on rolling daily returns) and technological similarities (hashing algorithms and proof types). They develop a dynamic covariate-assisted spectral clustering (CASC) method to identify latent crypto communities. Finally, they test portfolio diversification across communities and an inter-crypto momentum trading strategy that buys top-quartile and sells bottom-quartile momentum signal portfolios within communities.
extraction.universe: Top 400 cryptocurrencies by market capitalization as of December 31, 2018, filtered to 182 cryptocurrencies after excluding those under 1 year old or with incomplete contract/price data.

performance_metrics.context: Community 1 30-day-ahead return correlation difference between within- and cross-community (Dynamic CASC)
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The correlation difference is 2.8%, which is significant at the 1% level with a Newey–West adjusted t-statistic of 9.0.

performance_metrics.context: One-day-ahead average daily return of the inter-crypto momentum long-short portfolio (Winner-Loser)
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: It shows that the trading strategy generates a one-day-ahead average daily return of 1.08%, and the return does not revert in a week.

performance_metrics.context: t-statistic for the one-day-ahead average daily return of the inter-crypto momentum portfolio (Winner-Loser)

key_findings: Dynamic covariate-assisted spectral clustering (CASC) successfully recovers crypto network communities by combining return cross-predictability and technological similarities.
Investors achieve better risk diversification by investing in cross-community cryptocurrencies, evidenced by significantly lower return correlations across communities than within communities.
An inter-crypto momentum trading strategy based on community network linkages earns a robust one-day-ahead average daily return of 1.08% that does not revert within a week.

Behavioral factors such as market frictions (limit-to-arbitrage), investor attention, and economic policy uncertainty do not explain the momentum spillover effects, confirming an information propagation mechanism.
